reviews.title: Nguyễn Như Mai · IELTS 48 · W09 · Đề 1
reviews.scopeMarkdown: Bài gốc: **228 từ**, đếm bằng cách tách nguyên văn theo khoảng trắng; đủ tối thiểu 150 từ nhưng vượt khung 150–200 từ của lớp 28 từ. Cô chỉ chấm Đề 1 đã gõ; chưa chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Em cần sửa và nộp lại. Bài này em làm còn ẩu ở những chỗ cụ thể: cuối Detail 1 thiếu dấu chấm, còn “Italy also rose” và “France increased sharply” đều dùng tên nước làm chủ thể tăng. Overview gọi diễn biến của France là trái ngược cũng chưa đúng khi xét đầu–cuối kỳ. Em đã chia đủ năm nước và có dùng cấu trúc đã học, nhưng bài còn dài và thiếu nhận xét thấp nhất trong Overview. Cô yêu cầu em đọc lại kiến thức, tự sửa các câu đánh dấu và chọn mốc gọn hơn trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em đặt Germany–Italy–France trong Detail 1 và United Kingdom–Belgium trong Detail 2. Hai nhóm có tỷ lệ phần trăm cao hơn và thấp hơn ở cuối kỳ, nên Cô giữ cả nhóm lẫn thứ tự của em. Em làm rõ vị trí dẫn đầu của France năm 2004, mức bằng nhau của hai nước còn lại năm 2012 và rút mốc theo C07.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given  line chart illustrates how much the percentage of female members of parliament in five European countries was from 2000 to 2012.
Overall, there was a general increase in the percentages of female members of parliament, with Italy and the UK experiencing the most pronounced rises, while an opposite trend was observed in France. Also of note is that Germany had the highest percentage in 2000, whereas Italy recorded the highest figure in 2012.
To elaborate, in 2000, Germany had the highest percentage, at about 33%. Italy and France followed, with around 26% and 25% respectively. The figure for Germany increased gradually and reached about 37% in 2012. Italy also rose during the period, from approximately 26% in 2000 to 30% in 2004 and 33% in 2008. It then reached around 39% in 2012. France increased sharply to about 37% in 2004. However, it fell to around 29% in 2008 before rising slightly to approximately 32% in 2012
Regarding the remaining figures, the UK started with the lowest figure, at only about 3% in 2000. It then increased to 8% in 2004 and 20% in 2008, before reaching around 28% in 2012. Belgium also showed an increase, from about 17% in 2000 to 28% in 2004. After that, the figure stayed almost the same at around 29% in 2008 and then fell slightly to 28% in 2012.

Overall, the percentages of female members of parliament increased from start to finish in all five countries, most markedly in the United Kingdom. Germany initially had the highest figure, whereas Italy led in 2012; the United Kingdom remained lowest, sharing this position with Belgium at the end.

To elaborate, in 2000, about 33% of members of parliament in Germany were women, with a subsequent slight rise to 37% in 2012. The figure for Italy also rose, from 26% to 39% over the same period. That for France increased from 25% to a peak of 37% in 2004, briefly ranking first, before falling and then recovering to 31% in 2012.

Regarding the remaining figures, the percentage of female members of parliament in the United Kingdom climbed from 3% in 2000 to 28% in 2012. The figure for Belgium also increased, from 17% to 28% between 2000 and 2004, after which it remained relatively stable until 2012.

The given table illustrates the percentages of population aged 65 and above in three countries, including Canada, Germany and the UK, in 1988, 2000 and predictions for 2030.

Overall, there was a general increase in the percentage of old people in all three countries. Germany recorded the highest figures, while the opposite trend was observed in the UK, which had the lowest figures. Also of note is that the figures of all countries are expected to increase by 2030.

To elaborate, Germany started at 20.35% in 1988 and experienced a rise to 25.53% in 2000, before increasing further to a predicted 30.65% in 2030. Similarly, the figure for Canada increased from 16.45% to 20.65% between 1988 and 2000, and is forecasted to reach 26.35% in 2030.

Regarding the country with the lowest figures, the UK accounted for 14.25% in 1988, then increased slightly to 14.80% in 2000, before rising considerably to 20.45% in 2030. Although the UK remained the lowest throughout the period, it is expected to have a significant increase in the elderly population.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given bar chart illustrates the annual pay, in thousands of US dollars, for doctors and other workers in seven countries in 2004.
Overall, doctors were paid much more than other workers in all countries. The US had the highest salary for doctors, while Finland had the lowest salary of doctors. It can also be seen that the difference between two groups were biggest in the US.
To elaborate, doctors in the US earned about 120 thousand dollars, which was the highest number in the chart. Switzerland and France were the next countries, with 70 thousand dollars each. The figures for Germany and Czech Republic were around 63 thousand, while Italy was slightly lower, at 60 thousand. Finally, Finland had the lowest payment for doctors, with about 49 thousand dollars.
Regarding other workers, the US also had the highest pay, at around 45 thousand dollars, followed by Switzerland with 40 thousand. France and Finland were about 29 and 27 thousand dollars respectively. Italy, Czech Republic and Germany had almost the same salary, at 20 thousand dollars. In general, the salary of other workers were much lower comparing with doctors in all seven countries.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table illustrates the percentage of first-year students who gave a “very good” rating for the resources provided by the college in three courses.

Overall, Commerce had the highest figures in most categories, while Law had lower percentages. Teaching was rated the highest in Economics, while other resources got the highest percentage in Law.

To elaborate, the percentage of students who rated teaching very good was the same in Economics and Commerce, at 95%. However, Commerce had a higher figure for pre-course information, at 95%, compared with only 59% in Economics. For tutors, the figure of Commerce was 93%, slightly higher than Economics, at 90%. In addition, printed resources in Commerce were rated 85%, while Economics was 81%.

Regarding Law, pre-course information accounted for 72%, which was higher than teaching, at 62%. The figures for tutors and printed resources were 76% and 70%, respectively. Other resources had the highest percentage in Law, at 80%, but this was still lower than Commerce, at 81%. In general, Law had lower ratings than the other two courses in most categories.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table illustrates the number of universities ranked in the world's top 200 in three subjects in five countries in 2011.

Overall, the USA had the highest figures in all three subjects, while New Zealand had the lowest numbers. Biology was the most popular subject in the USA and the UK, while Psychology had the highest figures in Australia and Canada.

To elaborate, the USA had 69 universities in Biology, 54 in Medicine and 58 in Psychology. The figures for the UK were much lower, at 30, 24 and 29, respectively. It can be seen that the USA had more than twice as many universities as the UK in all three subjects.

Regarding Australia, New Zealand and Canada, Australia and Canada both had 9 universities in Biology, compared with 6 in New Zealand. For Medicine, Australia had 13 universities, followed by Canada with 12, while New Zealand had only 2. In Psychology, Australia had the highest figure, at 17, followed by Canada with 14 and New Zealand with just 4.
